points.t: Itchy, ill-defined, dry or weeping patches in the flexures (child/adult) or on the cheeks (infant); a personal or family history of atopy.
A leaky skin barrier plus Th2-driven inflammation, kept going by the itch–scratch cycle.
Emollient for everyone, every day. Add a topical steroid stepped to severity and body site.
Eczema herpeticum: punched-out erosions in an unwell patient. Admit the same day.

points: **Barrier defect.** Filaggrin-related dryness and a disordered lipid layer increase water loss and let irritants and allergens in.
**Immune dysregulation.** Th2-skewed inflammation drives the itch.
**Triggers:** soaps and detergents, *S. aureus*, allergens, heat, wool, climate and stress.
**Scratching** perpetuates the cycle, causing lichenification and secondary infection.

visuals.caption: The barrier–inflammation–itch cycle in atopic eczema. A defective stratum corneum lets water out and irritants and allergens in, which drives immune activation, itch and scratching.

items.name: Acute atopic flare
items.t: Red, weeping, vesicles or crust; intense itch

items.name: Chronic atopic
items.t: Dry, scaly, lichenified, excoriated; pigment change

items.name: Infant
items.t: Red, rough cheeks, scalp and trunk; nappy area often spared

items.name: Adult
items.t: Flexural or diffuse; hand and nipple eczema common

items.name: Irritant contact
items.t: Dry, fissured or red, sore skin at exposure sites

items.name: Allergic contact
items.t: Eczema matching the contact pattern; may spread

points: onset and course, triggers, occupation and hobbies, products used on the skin, response to past treatment, sleep and quality of life.
look at the whole skin for excoriation, lichenification and infection; check nails and eyes.
the diagnosis is uncertain or treatment fails. Consider **patch testing** for suspected contact allergy, a swab if infection is suspected or recurrent, and rarely a biopsy.
EASI and SCORAD are specialist and audit tools. In practice, grade as mild, moderate or severe using area, itch, sleep loss, exudate and thickening.

cards.name: Psoriasis
cards.clue: Well-demarcated plaques with silvery scale on extensors and scalp; usually less itchy; nail pitting

cards.name: Seborrhoeic dermatitis
cards.clue: Greasy yellow scale on scalp, nasolabial folds, eyebrows and chest

cards.name: Tinea corporis
cards.clue: Asymmetrical annular plaque with an active scaly edge; scrapings positive

cards.name: Scabies
cards.clue: Intense itch, worse at night; burrows in web spaces, wrists and genitals; itchy contacts

cards.name: Contact vs atopic
cards.clue: Contact eczema matches exposure in time and place, is often asymmetrical, and may be occupational

cards.name: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (rare)
cards.clue: Persistent, atypical plaques in an older adult; refer if anything seems odd

items.t: **Suspected eczema herpeticum:** clustered punched-out erosions or vesicles, often with fever. Needs **same-day hospital assessment** and aciclovir.
Severe or spreading infection, or a systemically unwell patient.
Severe disease not controlled after about a week of appropriate stepped treatment.
Diagnostic uncertainty, recurrent deep infections, or a major psychosocial impact.
Possible need for phototherapy or systemic treatment, or occupational disease needing workplace advice.

pearls.t: **Prescribe enough emollient.** Adults often need several hundred grams a month, and under-prescribing is the commonest reason treatment fails. Apply in the direction of hair growth, ideally after bathing while the skin is still damp.
**Fire risk:** dressings, clothing and bedding soaked in paraffin-based (and other) emollients can catch fire easily. Warn patients to keep away from naked flames.
Teach **fingertip units** (FTUs) so steroid doses are understood.
Tackle **steroid phobia** with clear advice on potency, site and duration. Under-treatment and rebound are far more common than harm.
**Inflamed is not the same as infected.** Weeping crust does not automatically mean an antibiotic.
**Pregnancy:** most emollients and mild to moderate steroids are acceptable. Check the BNF for each product.
Counselling: eczema is not caused by poor hygiene, and the barrier tendency is lifelong even when the skin is clear.
Hands and feet: see [hand eczema](condition:hand-eczema) for occupational dermatitis, pompholyx and patch-test referral.
